doc.title: Dave Valentin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Tito Puente's Grammy story and Latin influence in pop
summary: A story of Puente expecting to lose a Grammy and then winning, and Valentin's view of the Latin surge in popular music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I overheard you telling a humorous story about him at the Grammy awards.

Yeah. He thought he was not going to win. And he was downstairs and he was like that going, “I ain’t going to win nothin. All the Cubans are going to win.” And he actually won. And to make it short, and he told me, “And I had to run down five miles to get my Grammy.” They put me in the tenth tier. He walked out very sad out of the hotel and came back like a little kid. And I’m glad, I said, “Pop, I’m glad you won.” Because he was depressed he was not going to win, he just went there because Santana, you know, all that stuff.
There seems to be a pretty big surge in popular music with Latin influences.
Does that impact at all on what you do?
Yeah I think it has made people more aware of the rhythms and different contexts. I think it’s a good thing. Whether it’s because of the Buena Vista or — I think it helps everyone.
